name: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc.
business: Reynolds sells Reynolds Wrap foil, Hefty trash and storage bags, disposable tableware and store-brand equivalents to US grocers, mass merchants and clubs.

events.what: CEO and President (internal promotion from CFO); Lance Mitchell retires
events.from: Reynolds CFO since November 2023; before that CFO of SunOpta and Claire's Stores
Reynolds VP Financial Planning and Analysis since 2021

events.what: Director added, board 8 to 9 (son-in-law of controlling holder Graeme Hart, PFL)
Operating segments realigned into Hefty Waste and Clean-Up, Hefty Storage and Organization, Reynolds Cooking and Kitchen Essentials, Hefty Home and Tableware

events.from: ex CEO SIG Group; Apollo senior advisor

next_event.source: No Investor Day or framework update found in Baba 2025 to 2026 transcripts; Q3 2026 earnings call date not stated. Huckins's amended employment agreement term ends 2026-12-31 (8-K 0001193125-24-246994), no successor or extension announced.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: No margin target, rate or savings figure with a horizon. Only one-year absolute guides: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA $660M to $675M and revenue +1% to +3%. CFO says July pricing will be 'a numerical headwind to margin rate' in H2 2026. Margin is driven by aluminum and resin costs ($400M annualized commodity headwind, about 10% of revenue).

statements.quote: We now expect approximately $400 million of commodity headwinds on an annualized basis, up from $200 million when we reported in April, reflecting changes in commodity rates from the end of March to where markets settled at the end of June.
statements.speaker: Nathan Lowe
statements.doc_title: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: Productivity gains from lean deployment and automation are expanding margins. The savings they generate help fund reinvestment back into the business.
statements.speaker: Nathan Lowe
statements.doc_title: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: What remains true in the back half of the year is we've continued to focus on those productivity initiatives that will drive profitability, but I would expect the incremental pricing that's taking effect in July to be a numerical headwind to margin rate.
statements.speaker: Nathan Lowe
statements.doc_title: Reynolds Consumer Products Inc Q2 2026 Earnings Call

street.gap_assumption: No management margin target, so no gap. Calendar fiscal year, Baba FY labels equal company years. Consensus EBITDA FY2026 $667.7M (inside the $660M to $675M guide), FY2027 $694.5M, FY2028 $717.2M.

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin yoy: Q4 2025 +41 bps, Q1 2026 +63 bps. VA has not loaded Q2 2026; per Huckins H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA $302M (+8%) on revenue of $1.8B (+4%), and per Lowe H1 gross margin +120 bps (doc 110804). LTM 18.04% uses Q2 2025 to Q1 2026.

disqualifier_reason: Catalyst older than 18 months with no pending change: Huckins (internal, ex CFO) and CFO Lowe both took office 2025-01-01, 21 months ago; in-window items are a controlling-holder board seat and a segment realignment. Margin is also commodity driven (aluminum and resin, $400M annualized headwind passed through by pricing), and management has given no numeric margin framework.
verdict: Cheap, controlled foil and bag maker with stable estimates, but the CEO change is 21 months old, internal, and margins track aluminum and resin with no target.
open_questions: Is Huckins's employment agreement (term ends 2026-12-31) extended, or is a further CEO change coming?
Does management ever set a margin or productivity savings target, or stay with one-year EBITDA dollar guides?
How much of the H1 2026 gross margin gain reverses as July pricing on the $400M commodity headwind flows through?
